sections.title: People & Politics
sections.description: Important developments in governments, societies and the people shaping the world.

cards.title: Thames Valley Police Admits Warrants to Investigate Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor Were Unlawful
cards.content: Thames Valley Police has admitted that the search warrants used to investigate Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor's homes were unlawful. The warrants were issued after he was arrested in February on suspicion of misconduct in public office. The police seized documents and electronic devices from his homes and now a judge will decide if they can keep the evidence.

cards.title: Two Latvian men arrested at RAF Molesworth for trespass and security breach.
cards.content: Two Latvian men aged 36 and 32 were arrested at RAF Molesworth in Cambridgeshire after a fence was breached. The alert was raised when an abandoned vehicle was found near the base and searches revealed a small breach in the perimeter fence. The men were initially arrested for trespass and damage then further arrested under the National Security Act for allegedly entering the base for a purpose prejudicial to the UK. Counter-terror police are investigating but don't think it's connected to a recent incident at RAF Fairford.

cards.title: Anne Carson Wins Nobel Prize in Literature
cards.content: Canadian poet Anne Carson has won this year's Nobel Prize in Literature. The 76-year-old is recognized for her unique writing style which often blends poetry fiction and scholarship. The Nobel Committee praised her bold and inventive work which playfully interacts with classical traditions to create new forms of contemporary literature. Carson was surprised but happy when she was told the news and is the first Canadian to win the prize. She has written many notable works including poetry collections and translations of ancient Greek plays. The Nobel Prize is considered the most prestigious award in global literature and comes with a prize of 12 million Swedish kronor.

sections.title: Science and technology
sections.description: Discover breakthroughs in science, space, computing and emerging technology.

cards.title: UK MP Sues US Tech Firm xAI Over AI-Generated Sexualized Images
cards.content: Jess Asato a UK MP is suing a US tech firm xAI over the creation of sexualized images of her using their AI chatbot tool Grok. She's seeking damages for the misuse of her private information and data protection breaches. xAI failed to show up at a New York City Council meeting to discuss regulating AI developers despite being subpoenaed. Asato says this shows the company's "level of arrogance" and believes that women are disproportionately affected by this type of AI-generated content.

cards.title: Manus AI Agent Startup Raises $500 Million Despite Meta Hiccup
cards.content: Manus an AI agent startup raised over $500 million in its first funding round since Meta dropped its acquisition plans. The round was led by private equity firm Boyu Capital and venture investor IDG Capital with follow-on investment from existing shareholders. This shows that investors aren't deterred by Beijing's order to block Meta's acquisition of Manus and suggests that the appetite for AI-agent startups remains strong.

cards.title: Amazon Launches New Tablets with Alexa, Priced $230 to $550
cards.content: Amazon has launched new tablets with Alexa priced between $230 and $550. The devices have improved speed artificial intelligence features and a higher-resolution display. Amazon is ditching its budget-friendly Fire lineup a significant shift in its devices strategy. The new tablets run Google's Android operating system unlike earlier models which used Amazon's own app store. The company hopes the pricier devices will encourage users to buy more products and services like movies and audiobooks from Amazon's webstore.

sections.title: Health & wellness
sections.description: Medical research, public health and discoveries that affect everyday wellbeing.

cards.title: Nigerian Paediatrician Elected President-Elect of Union for International Cancer Control
cards.content: Dr. Zainab Shinkafi-Bagudu a Nigerian paediatrician has been elected president-elect of the Union for International Cancer Control. She's the first African to lead the organisation and will take office at a time when cancer cases and deaths are expected to rise sharply especially in poorer countries. Bagudu's goal is to use her position to bring attention to the lack of cancer care in low-income countries and to find ways to improve access to cancer services including screening diagnosis and treatment. She wants to focus on prevention and early diagnosis as well as developing new approaches to cancer financing.

cards.title: Margaret Hamilton, NASA Apollo Software Pioneer, Dies at 90
cards.content: Margaret Hamilton a pioneering software engineer has died at 90. She was the leader of a team that developed the software for NASA's Apollo missions which helped put astronauts on the moon. Hamilton's work also helped establish the field of software engineering.

cards.title: WHO Investigates Death of Russian Lab Worker from Rare Plague
cards.content: The World Health Organization is trying to figure out what happened when a worker at a Russian lab died from a rare form of plague. The lab worker a 28-year-old woman was hospitalized and then died. Several hundred people who had contact with her are in quarantine. The WHO is concerned because the plague can spread from person to person. The organization is trying to get more information from Russia but has not received a response. The WHO has seen reports of a broken test tube in the lab but it's not clear if that's related to the worker's death.

sections.title: Environment
sections.description: Climate, oceans, ecosystems and the changing planet around us.

cards.title: India's Monsoon Ends 13% Below Average, Drought Hits Major States
cards.content: India's southwest monsoon ended 13% below average but some regions are experiencing severe drought conditions. States like Maharashtra Karnataka Rajasthan Andhra Pradesh and Telangana have formally declared drought with many farmers facing crop losses income losses and mounting debt. Despite decades of investment in water conservation and drought-proofing India's farm economy remains vulnerable to rainfall shocks. The drought has already led to failed crops fodder shortages and cattle sales at distress prices with some farmers struggling to make ends meet.

cards.title: Heavy rain and strong winds hit northern India, snowfall expected in Himalayan peaks
cards.content: Heavy rain hit Uttarakhand Himachal Pradesh and Jammu and Kashmir with strong winds while snowfall is expected in higher Himalayan peaks. In other parts of the country Kerala Tamil Nadu West Bengal and Sikkim are under heavy rainfall alerts with thunderstorms lightning and gusty winds possible. In Delhi-NCR mornings and nights are getting cooler but days are still hot with isolated thunderstorms and showers expected in some areas. Meanwhile Punjab Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh may see thunderstorms lightning and strong winds prompting weather authorities to issue cautionary alerts.

cards.title: Maharashtra declared drought-hit after one of India's driest monsoons
cards.content: Around 74% of Maharashtra a state in India was declared drought-hit after one of the driest monsoons in years. The government has directed local bodies to cut water usage by 10% from October 16 to conserve water. This comes amid concerns over limited water reserves which are linked to reduced rainfall. The state has also announced plans to reuse treated wastewater for various purposes such as gardening and industrial activities to manage water better.

sections.title: Entertainment
sections.description: Stories from film, music, sports, culture and the world of entertainment.

cards.title: BBC Announces Radio 4 Programme Cuts to Save £500m
cards.content: The BBC has announced plans to cut several Radio 4 programmes including You and Yours Thinking Allowed Free Thinking and others in order to make £500m savings. The corporation will also reduce commissioning on Radio 5 Live and its podcasts. However the BBC is investing in new consumer and ideas-based programmes. Radio 4's flagship show In Our Time will expand and Start the Week and Farming Today will also grow in length. The BBC says it's "reshaping" its speech audio to build a strong future for trusted journalism and distinctive storytelling.

cards.title: New Play Explores Struggles of Retired Boxers with Mental Health
cards.content: A new play called The Corner Man explores the struggles men face when they stop doing something they're passionate about like boxing. The story follows a fighter who has to adjust to life outside the ring after years of dedication. The play also looks at how men talk about their mental health or don't and how having a support network can help. The writer and producer Cathal J Ferris drew inspiration from his own experience with boxing and conversations with fighters.

cards.title: Gaten Matarazzo Stars in London's West End Production of Rock Musical Rent
cards.content: Gaten Matarazzo who's best known for playing Dustin Henderson in Stranger Things is now starring in the rock musical Rent on London's West End. He's having a change of pace from filming the hit Netflix show which he says was intense with only 30 takes to get it right. Matarazzo who's been acting since he was a kid enjoys the schedule and routine of theatre work saying it's a welcome change from the unpredictability of filming. He's been doing Rent for a while now and says it's a great experience with certain songs feeling relevant to today's world.

sections.title: economy
sections.description: Markets, businesses, trade and economic changes shaping the global economy.

cards.title: Alberta to Hold Referendum on Independence
cards.content: Alberta a western Canadian province is set to hold a referendum on October 19 where residents will decide whether to stay in Canada or move ahead with a formal binding referendum on independence. The province's economy is unique with rich oil and gas reserves a strong agricultural sector and a young and skilled workforce. Proponents of independence argue that the province would be richer on its own with more money kept within its borders. However opponents predict a more sober outcome warning of significant costs including a potential hit to Alberta's GDP additional debt and reduced disposable income for residents.

cards.title: Tui River Cruises faces backlash over changed itineraries
cards.content: Passengers who paid thousands of pounds for European river cruises with Tui are angry after their itineraries changed leaving them with hours spent on coach trips instead of sailing. Some have told the BBC they should get a refund but Tui has offered none. The company apologised blaming low water levels on the Danube and said customers continued their holidays on amended itineraries under standard booking conditions.

cards.title: Chrysler Building gets $235 million renovation for Art Deco crown restoration
cards.content: The Chrysler Building in Manhattan is getting a major renovation. The building which is over 90 years old will have its Art Deco crown restored and its 77-storey façade restored. The renovation will cost $235 million and will include upgrading the building's systems and adding a new lounge on the 61st floor. The building's owner the Cooper Union college will use the money from the sale to offer full-tuition scholarships to its students.
